title: Assistant Section Officer; Assistant Caretaker
qualification: The candidate must be a citizen of India. A separate application for each post is not needed: ticking the box beside the posts shown in the registration form makes the candidate an applicant for each ticked post, and only one fee is payable. || If two candidates are in contention for one post, the desirable qualification fixed for that post decides. The post-wise desirable qualification is given in the Schedule attached to the Bihar Vidhan Sabha Sachivalaya (Recruitment and Service Conditions) Rules, 2018. Candidates should check the official notification for the eligibility of each post.

title: IOCL Vacancy 2026 - 272 Trade Apprentice, Technician Apprentice PostsIOCL Vacancy 2026
qualification: It must be a regular full-time course from a recognised Board/University/Institute, with minimum 50% aggregate marks (45% for SC/ST and PwBD candidates for the seats reserved for them). || Where CGPA/OGPA or letter grade is awarded, the equivalent aggregate percentage must be entered in the Microsoft Form, and a certificate from the University/Institute is needed at Document Verification. || Only the branch or subjects specified against the trade count; no claim of an equivalent qualification is entertained. || Diploma holders under a recognised lateral entry scheme (Class XII (Sc.) or ITI admitted in the 2nd year of the Diploma course) are also eligible, subject to the prescribed percentage on the aggregate of all semesters. || A B.Sc candidate (Physics, Mathematics and Chemistry/Industrial Chemistry) may apply for only one of code 101 or 103. Applying for more than one trade leads to summary rejection.
salary: The stipend per month is as prescribed under the Apprentices Act, 1961/1973, the Apprentices Rules 1992 (as amended) and the Corporation's guidelines. Training lasts 12 months for codes 101, 105 and 107 and 24 months for code 103, and may be extended under Rule 7 of the Apprentices Rules 1992. || One pair of safety shoes and a helmet are provided, returnable on completion of training, wherever applicable. || No HRA or company accommodation is provided. || General leave is 32 days (8 days per quarter), including medical grounds. Casual leave is 12 days per calendar year (pro-rata). Holidays follow the establishment, and unavailed leave lapses at the end of the apprenticeship. || Apprentices are covered under suitable accident insurance and under the Certified Standing Orders applicable to workmen at the establishment.
age_limit: 18 to 24 years as on 30.11.2026 (General/EWS), with relaxation for reserved categories
selection_process: Selection runs through a merit list, Document Verification, pre-engagement medical examination and the offer of engagement. There is no written test.
